findings.rationale: MD's uploaded updates are anomalous in every round: norm about 4-5x the median client's, and cosine against the median update is strongly negative (mean -0.79 across 20 rounds, about -0.94 in round 1). This is consistent with a scaled, sign-flipped update. MD's local performance looks normal (AUC 0.82, CITL about 0.002), so the anomaly is in the uploads rather than in its data.

MI's updates are anomalous in every round: norm about 3-3.7x the median, and cosine against the median update is near -1 in early rounds (mean -0.79 across rounds). The pattern is consistent with a scaled, sign-flipped upload. MI's local AUC (0.80) and CITL (0.013) are normal, so its data and performance do not explain the anomaly.

MT's updates are anomalous across all rounds: norm about 2.6-3.3x the median, and cosine against the median update is strongly negative (mean -0.66 across rounds, -0.87 in round 1). The pattern is consistent with a scaled, sign-flipped upload. Its local AUC (0.80) and CITL (0.012) look normal.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with client_updates, client_performance, drift_by_round, feature_summary and subgroup_outcomes (Sex, AgeGroup, Income), then confirmed per round. Three clients (MD, MI, MT) show a consistent poisoning signature: norm ratios of about 3-5x the median and strongly negative cosine to the median update, from round 1 onward. Their local AUC and calibration are normal, so the fault is in the uploads, not the data. GU showed erratic per-round updates, but it is small (n=708), its deviations were about z=4 and not corroborated by performance, drift or subgroup tools, so I treated it as noise. Other screen outliers (feature-level tails at SD, NH, DC, FL; subgroup O/E ratios at FL, MD, SC, MS, WV, HI, MT, AL; drift at MI, LA, VI) were either under |z|=6, from small clients, or not corroborated by a second tool, so I did not report them. Budget was fully used (0.1 left).
